summary: The CREATIVE Act of 2025 amends the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 to create a competitive grant program administered by the Secretary of Commerce. Named the Creative Economy Revitalization and Workforce Development Program, it provides funding for hiring artists and personnel, constructing or acquiring arts facilities, and maintaining or improving existing facilities to increase job opportunities and access to arts programming.

affected_groups.effect: They may receive increased job opportunities, compensation, and full-time employment through funded productions, projects, performances, and exhibitions.
Eligible entities such as local arts agencies, museums, and nonprofit theaters can apply for competitive grants to hire staff, construct or acquire facilities, and perform maintenance.
Communities with limited access to arts facilities or programming receive priority for grant awards, and up to 25 percent of funds are reserved for rural areas.

key_provisions: Establishes three types of competitive grants: Hiring and production grants up to $5,000,000; Construction and acquisition grants up to $3,000,000; and Maintenance and improvement grants up to $3,000,000.
Prohibits any eligible entity from receiving more than one grant under the program.

Requires grant applicants to submit detailed information on community outreach, low-income and underrepresented community representation, and attestations that they will not abrogate collective bargaining agreements and will abide by labor standards.
Prioritizes entities located in communities with limited arts access, those serving diverse or minority populations, those experiencing financial hardship, and those in rural communities.
Authorizes appropriations of $700,000,000 for each of the fiscal years 2026 through 2030, with up to 25 percent reserved for rural communities.
Requires annual reports from grant recipients describing how funds were used and their effects on access to arts facilities and employment.
missing_information: Total actual appropriations may differ from authorized amounts depending on future congressional action.
Specific operational rules and application deadlines to be set by the Secretary of Commerce are not detailed.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The CREATIVE Act of 2025 amends the Public Works and Economic Development Act of 1965 to create a competitive grant program administered by the Secretary of Commerce. Named the Creative Economy Revitalization and Workforce Development Program, it provides funding for hiring artists and personnel, constructing or acquiring arts facilities, and maintaining or improving existing facilities to increase job opportunities and access to arts programming.
summary_detail.significance: This bill establishes a federal grant program with an authorization of $700,000,000 annually from fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to support the creative economy, arts employment, and facility improvements nationwide.
